rubrics.justification: The response incorrectly states there is no lab morphology description and declines to use the provided Gardner 3AA score. It fails to describe the known morphology (expanded blastocyst, high-quality ICM and TE, thinning zona) and instead discusses hypothetical Day 4 features.

It integrates most relevant factors well, including age-related aneuploidy risk, ovarian reserve, prior live birth, semen quality, BMI, endometrium, and transfer timing, though it does not connect these to the known strong 3AA morphology.
The reasoning is generally structured and logical, but it is undermined by the central inconsistency of ignoring the provided Gardner 3AA grade while basing prognosis on morphology being unknown.

Most recommendations are broadly consistent with IVF practice (single embryo transfer preference, luteal support, considering blastocyst culture/PGT-A selectively), but rejecting the provided Gardner score because transfer was on Day 4 is not well aligned with standard use of documented embryo grading data.

Provides practical next steps for transfer management and future cycle review, including embryology data to request and when to consider blastocyst culture or PGT-A, though recommendations would be stronger if tailored to the known 3AA embryo quality.
